newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends sharply up in short covering rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends sharply up in short covering rally.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil rallied Tuesday, sending oil prices surging, as heating oil's May contract expiry approached amid tight supplies, triggering short covering.
"There was a lot of talk of a short squeeze because someone may be taking a large delivery," said Nauman Barakat, trader with Prudential Securities, of the heating oil rally.
May heating oil ended up 2.38 cents a gallon at 58.91 cents. June crude finished up 53 cents at $20.44 a barrel while May gasoline ended up 1.02 cents a gallon at 63.36 cents.

Cash supplies of heating oil in the New York Harbor have been tight after unseasonably cold weather in the northeastern United States drained refinery stocks. The region is the largest heating oil market in the world.
With the May heating oil contract expiring Wednesday amid short supply, traders bought themselves out of their short positions which would have obligated them to deliver heating oil.
Moreover, several dealers said Vitol SA was expected to take a large delivery of heating oil on the May contract creating even more pressure to cover one's short position.
Vitol declined comment on the talk.
On the charts, June crude rose to a session high of $20.49, breaking resistance of of $20.25, a level set by June's session high $20.27, its highest level since April 2.
But, June crude's sharp move kept intact a trendline on the spot chart extending from the session high January 31 of $24.87 through the session high March 20 of $22.50.

After the market's close, American Petroleum Institute (API) released oil inventory data for the week ended April 25. Gasoline stocks fell 408,000 barrels and distillate stocks drew 1.4 million barrels, both declining as traders expected.
But, crude stocks grew 1.9 million barrels when dealers had expected a one million barrel decline.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
